newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela faction calls for halt in oil opening.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela faction calls for halt in oil opening.

text.p: Venezuela's Senate Environment Committee leader called on the government Wednesday to halt foreign oil company operations in the eastern Delta Amacuro region while the Committee investigates allegations of environmental damage.
Lucia Antillano, of opposition union-based party Radical Cause, also called for the suspension of oil exploration licensing in the Orinoco Delta, which is home to about 25,000 Warao indians.

In a press release, Antillano said the Committee had received a report from pressure group Survival International describing how foreign companies were polluting the Delta's fragile ecosystem and threatening the Warao way of life with extinction.

"We are calling on the National Executive to halt the activities of these foreign companies and to suspend approval of the sale of rights to other companies which want to work in the Orinoco Delta and Paria state," the statement said.
It named Amoco, Benton Oil and Gas, British Petroleum, Louisiana Land and Exploration and Norcen which all have contracts in the region.
Antillano announced an investigation into the companies' activities to see whether they contravened the country's constitution.
Venezuelan pressure groups have previously called for oil companies to leave the Delta, but this is the first time a congress leader has backed them.

Corporacion Venezolana de Petroleos (CVP), the subsidiary of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela which has awarded licences to the foreign companies, said recently the Warao indians were in talks with the oil companies.
Contrary to pressure group claims, CVP spokesman Freddy Muziotti said the Warao have not asked the companies to leave.

"There are a lot of people who are holding up the Warao as a flag to take revenge for old grudges," Muzotti said. "They are trying to represent the Warao, but none of these international organisations can represent the Warao because the Warao have not given them the right to."
